topics.name: Running Experiments
topics.description: evaluate(), repetitions, dataset splits and versions in LangSmith.
notes: ## 实验与 evaluate()
- 实验（experiment）是某个应用版本在数据集上的评估结果，记录每个样例的输出、evaluator 分数和执行 trace。
- 同一数据集上通常会跑多个实验，用来比较不同提示词或模型配置。
- `evaluate()` / `client.evaluate()` 的核心参数：target、data、evaluators。
- target：接收输入字典（example.inputs）并返回输出字典的函数。
- data：数据集名称或 UUID，也可以是样例迭代器。
- 可选参数：experiment_prefix、description、metadata、max_concurrency、num_repetitions。
```python
results = client.evaluate(
target,
data="qa-basic",
evaluators=[correct],
experiment_prefix="baseline",
max_concurrency=4,
num_repetitions=3,
- max_concurrency 通过多线程并行处理数据集，大型评估任务建议设置。
- metadata 中的保留键 models / prompts / tools 会填充实验表对应的列，便于分组和过滤。
## 重复运行
- num_repetitions=N 让每个样例运行 N 次；5 个样例 × 5 次 = 25 次运行。
- LLM 输出不确定，重复运行可降低噪声；UI 显示平均分，并可查看多次运行的标准差。
## 数据集组织
- Example 由 inputs、可选的 reference outputs 和可选的 metadata 组成；reference outputs 不会传给应用，只供 evaluator 使用。
- Splits 是命名子集：可按训练/验证/测试、按类别或分阶段上线来划分；一个样例可以属于多个 split。
- Versions：样例变化时自动创建版本，可打标签；CI 中指定版本可避免数据集更新破坏流程。

topics.name: Custom, Summary and Pairwise Evaluators
topics.description: Writing code, summary, LLM-as-judge and pairwise evaluators.
notes: ## 代码 evaluator
- evaluator 函数的参数名固定，可取以下任意子集：run、example、inputs、outputs、reference_outputs。
- 大多数场景只需要 inputs、outputs、reference_outputs。
- 返回值：dict（key 加 score 或 value）、int/float/bool、str、list[dict]（一个函数返回多个指标）。
- 直接返回 int/float/bool 时按连续指标处理，函数名作为指标名；str 为分类指标。
- dict 中 score 用于数值指标，value 用于分类指标。
```python
def correct(outputs: dict, reference_outputs: dict) -> bool:
return outputs["answer"] == reference_outputs["answer"]
## Summary evaluator
- 有些指标只能在整个实验上计算，例如整体通过率或 F1。
- Summary evaluator 的参数是列表：outputs: list[dict]、reference_outputs: list[dict] 等。
- 通过 evaluate(..., summary_evaluators=[...]) 传入，结果以对应 key 显示在 UI 中。
## LLM-as-judge
- 评分规则写在提示词里，可以是无参考（reference-free）或基于参考（reference-based）。
- 需要检查分数并调整提示词；加入输入、输出和期望评分的 few-shot 示例通常能提升效果。
- LangSmith 可收集对 evaluator 分数的人工修正，并自动作为 few-shot 示例插入提示词。
## Pairwise evaluator
- 对两个已有实验的输出做对比，而不是重新运行应用：evaluate(("exp-a", "exp-b"), evaluators=[...])。
- evaluator 的 outputs 是包含两个输出的列表；返回两项分数列表时，顺序与 outputs 一致，函数名作为 feedback key。
- randomize_order=True 随机化输出顺序，用来减轻位置偏差。

topics.name: Trajectory and RAG Evaluation
topics.description: agentevals trajectory matching and the four RAG evaluators.
notes: ## Agent 轨迹评估（agentevals）
- 轨迹（trajectory）是 agent 执行的完整消息序列，包括 tool calls。
- 两种方式：trajectory match（与硬编码的参考轨迹逐步比较）和 LLM-as-judge。
- Trajectory match 确定、快速、无额外 LLM 成本，适合流程明确的场景。
```python
from agentevals.trajectory.match import create_trajectory_match_evaluator
evaluator = create_trajectory_match_evaluator(
trajectory_match_mode="superset",
- strict：消息和 tool calls 的顺序完全一致，但允许消息文本不同。
- unordered：tool calls 相同，顺序不限。
- subset：agent 只调用参考轨迹中出现的工具，不能多调用。
- superset：agent 至少调用参考中的工具，允许额外调用。
- 轨迹 LLM-as-judge（create_trajectory_llm_as_judge）可以不提供参考轨迹，也可使用带参考的提示词。
## RAG 评估
- Correctness：回答对比参考答案，需要数据集中有参考答案。
- Relevance：回答对比输入，不需要参考答案。
- Groundedness：回答对比检索到的文档，检查是否有幻觉，不需要参考答案。
- Retrieval relevance：检索文档对比问题，不需要参考答案。
- evaluator 要访问文档，target 就必须把 documents 放进返回的输出。
- 评分 schema 中把 explanation 字段放在布尔结果之前，模型按字段顺序生成，会先推理再给结论。

topics.name: Pytest, Annotation Queues and Online Evaluators
topics.description: Regression tests in CI, human review queues and online evaluators.
notes: ## pytest 集成
- 用 @pytest.mark.langsmith 标记测试；每个测试同步为一个数据集样例，每次运行生成一个实验。
- 默认记录 pass 布尔反馈；可用 t.log_inputs / log_outputs / log_reference_outputs / log_feedback 补充。
- 参数化时，默认所有参数记为 inputs，用 output_keys 指定哪些参数是参考输出。
```python
@pytest.mark.langsmith(output_keys=["expected"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("query, expected", [("hi", "hello")])
def test_greet(query, expected):
assert greet(query) == expected
- 环境变量：LANGSMITH_TEST_SUITE（测试套件名）、LANGSMITH_EXPERIMENT（实验名）、LANGSMITH_EXPERIMENT_METADATA（JSON 元数据）。
- LANGSMITH_TEST_CACHE 把 HTTP 请求缓存到磁盘，节省 CI 成本；LANGSMITH_TEST_TRACKING=false 只本地运行，不上传结果。
## 人工反馈：Annotation queues
- 单运行队列：一次审阅一个 run 或 thread，按评分细则（rubric）提交反馈。
- Pairwise 队列：从数据集中选择恰好两个实验创建，并排比较 Run A 和 Run B。
- 可通过 Add to Dataset 把审阅过的 run 存为数据集样例。
- 设置多个 reviewer 时，reviewer 看不到其他人的反馈，但评论对所有人可见。
## 在线 evaluator
- 作用于生产 trace（runs 和 threads），没有 reference outputs。
- 可用过滤条件限定触发范围，sampling rate 控制过滤后运行的评估比例（0.1 即 10%）。
- 回填（backfill）历史 runs 只能在创建规则时设置。

questions.title: In client.evaluate(), which argument tells LangSmith which dataset to run the target function over?

options.text: target
data
metadata
experiment_prefix

questions.explanation: The data argument takes the dataset name or UUID (or an iterator of examples). target is the function being evaluated, and experiment_prefix only names the experiment.

questions.title: How are the reference outputs of a dataset example used during an experiment?

options.text: They are passed to the target function together with the inputs
They are only used by evaluators and are not passed to the application
They are appended to the system prompt
They are used as few-shot examples for the target model

questions.explanation: Reference outputs are not passed to the application; evaluators read them to compare against the actual outputs. Only example inputs reach the target function.

questions.title: Fill in the blank so that each example in the dataset is run three times.
questions.codeSnippet:
results = client.evaluate(
    target,
    data="qa-basic",
    evaluators=[correct],
    experiment_prefix="baseline",
    ______=3,
)

options.text: max_concurrency
repetitions
num_repetitions
num_runs

questions.explanation: num_repetitions sets how many times each example is evaluated. max_concurrency only controls parallelism, not the number of runs per example.

questions.title: The dataset has 5 examples. How many target runs does this experiment produce?
questions.codeSnippet:
results = evaluate(
    target,
    data="qa-basic",
    evaluators=[correct],
    num_repetitions=5,
)
questions.explanation: Each of the 5 examples is run 5 times, giving 25 runs. Repetitions multiply the runs rather than adding to them.

questions.title: Which are common ways to use dataset splits in LangSmith?

options.text: ML-style training, validation and test subsets to avoid overfitting
Category-based subsets to evaluate different input types separately
A staged rollout that keeps exploratory examples isolated from the main evaluation set
Enforcing that every example belongs to exactly one split, since multiple splits are not allowed

questions.explanation: Splits are named subsets for ML-style, category-based or staged-rollout grouping. LangSmith does allow an example to belong to multiple splits, so option D is wrong.

questions.title: This evaluation fails when the evaluator runs. What is the problem?

options.text: evaluate() requires experiment_prefix to be set
Evaluators are not allowed to read reference_outputs
The target should take the example's inputs dict and return an output dict such as {"answer": ...}
data must be a dataset UUID, not a name

questions.explanation: The target function receives the inputs dictionary and must return a dictionary, which evaluators then index as outputs["answer"]. Here the target returns a plain string, so the evaluator cannot read it.

questions.title: Examples in a dataset keep changing, but a CI pipeline must not break when they do. What does LangSmith offer for this?

options.text: Dataset versions are created automatically when examples change; tag a version and target it in CI
Datasets are immutable once created, so examples cannot change
Metadata on each example freezes its content
Splits snapshot the dataset at the time they are created

questions.explanation: LangSmith creates dataset versions automatically when examples change, and versions can be tagged for important milestones. Splits and metadata organize examples but do not pin their content.

questions.title: A Python code evaluator named exact_match returns a bare bool. How is the result recorded?

options.text: As a continuous metric named after the function, exact_match
As a categorical metric named score
It is ignored unless a dict is returned
As a free-text comment on the run

questions.explanation: An int, float or bool return value is treated as a continuous metric, and the function name becomes the metric name. A dict is only needed to customize the key or use a categorical value.

questions.title: How many pieces of feedback does this evaluator log for each example?
questions.codeSnippet:
def check(outputs: dict, reference_outputs: dict) -> list[dict]:
    return [
        {"key": "correct",
         "score": outputs["answer"] == reference_outputs["answer"]},
        {"key": "concise",
         "score": len(outputs["answer"]) < 200},
    ]

options.text: 1, because the function has one name
0, because lists are not supported
2, one per dict in the list

questions.explanation: Returning list[dict] lets one evaluator log multiple metrics, one feedback entry per dict key. The function name is not used as the key when the dicts specify their own keys.

questions.title: Fill in the blank so that the evaluator logs a categorical metric.

options.text: "label"
"score"
"category"
"value"

questions.explanation: In an evaluator result dict, "score" is used for numerical metrics and "value" for categorical ones. label and category are not recognized keys.

questions.title: The goal is a single pass-rate metric for the whole experiment, but this logs one value per example. What is the fix?

options.text: Increase max_concurrency so results are aggregated
Set num_repetitions so the scores are averaged into one metric
Return a list of dicts instead of a single dict
Make it a summary evaluator that takes outputs and reference_outputs as lists and pass it via summary_evaluators

questions.explanation: Experiment-level metrics need a summary evaluator, which receives lists of outputs and reference outputs and is registered with summary_evaluators. A row-level evaluator is called once per example.

questions.title: How can LangSmith help align an LLM-as-a-judge evaluator with human preferences?

options.text: Collect human corrections on evaluator scores, which are inserted into the prompt as few-shot examples
Raise the judge model's temperature so it explores more grading styles
Remove the reference output from the prompt
Switch the evaluator to a code evaluator

questions.explanation: With few-shot enabled, human corrections to evaluator scores are automatically added to the judge prompt as examples. The other options do not use human feedback to calibrate the judge.

questions.title: Which statements about running a pairwise evaluation with evaluate() are correct?

options.text: The target is a list of two existing experiments, given as names or UUIDs
randomize_order=True randomizes output order to reduce positional bias
The outputs argument of the evaluator is a two-item list of outputs
It re-runs the application on the dataset for both versions

questions.explanation: Pairwise evaluation compares outputs of experiments that already exist; it does not execute the application again.

questions.title: For an example where exp-a's answer is shorter than exp-b's, what does this pairwise evaluator log?
questions.codeSnippet:
def ranked_preference(inputs: dict, outputs: list[dict]) -> list:
    a = outputs[0]["answer"]
    b = outputs[1]["answer"]
    return [1, 0] if len(a) <= len(b) else [0, 1]

evaluate(("exp-a", "exp-b"), evaluators=[ranked_preference])

options.text: Key ranked_preference: 0 for exp-a and 1 for exp-b
Key score: 1 for exp-b
Key ranked_preference: 1 for exp-a and 0 for exp-b
An error, because evaluate() needs a data argument

questions.explanation: A two-item list of scores follows the order of outputs, so index 0 belongs to exp-a. The function name becomes the feedback key.

questions.title: Which agentevals trajectory_match_mode requires the same tool calls as the reference but allows them in any order?

options.text: strict
subset
superset
unordered

questions.explanation: unordered accepts the same tool calls in any order. strict also enforces the order of messages and tool calls.

questions.title: The reference trajectory only calls get_weather. The agent must call it but may also call extra tools. Which mode fills the blank?

options.text: strict
unordered
subset
superset

questions.explanation: superset requires at least the reference tool calls and permits extras. subset is the opposite: the agent may call only tools that appear in the reference.

questions.title: What score does this evaluation produce?
questions.codeSnippet:
evaluator = create_trajectory_match_evaluator(
    trajectory_match_mode="strict",
)
# actual: Human -> AI(tool_call get_weather city="SF")
#         -> Tool -> AI("It is sunny in SF.")
# reference: the same four messages and tool call, but the
#         final AI text is "The weather in SF is sunny."
result = evaluator(outputs=actual, reference_outputs=reference)
print(result["score"])

options.text: True, because strict mode allows differences in message content
False, because the final message text differs
False, because strict mode requires an LLM judge
An error, because the trajectories differ

questions.explanation: strict mode requires identical messages and tool calls in the same order, but it allows the message content to differ. It does not call an LLM.

questions.title: Which RAG evaluator checks whether an answer is justified by the retrieved documents, without needing a reference answer?

options.text: Correctness
Relevance
Groundedness
Retrieval relevance

questions.explanation: Groundedness compares the response to the retrieved documents to detect hallucinations. Correctness needs a reference answer, and retrieval relevance compares documents to the question.

questions.title: Which RAG evaluators do not need a reference answer in the dataset?

options.text: Correctness (response vs reference answer)
Relevance (response vs input)
Groundedness (response vs retrieved docs)
Retrieval relevance (retrieved docs vs input)

questions.explanation: Only correctness compares the response to a reference answer. The other three compare artifacts produced by the run itself.

questions.title: The groundedness evaluator raises a KeyError. What is the cause?

options.text: The target does not return the retrieved documents in its outputs
Groundedness evaluators must take reference_outputs
retriever.invoke cannot be used inside an evaluation target
The evaluator must be async

questions.explanation: The evaluator only sees what the target returns, so the target must include the retrieved documents, for example {"answer": ..., "documents": docs}. Groundedness needs no reference answer.

questions.title: In a structured grade schema for an LLM judge, why is the explanation field placed before the boolean result?

options.text: Fields are generated in the order they are defined, so reasoning comes before the final verdict
LangSmith rejects schemas that put booleans first
The explanation is used as the feedback key
It lets the judge skip reading the reference answer

questions.explanation: The model generates fields in the defined order, so putting the explanation first makes it reason before committing to a verdict. The tutorial notes this ordering explicitly.

questions.title: Which decorator marks a pytest test so that it is tracked as a LangSmith example and experiment result?

options.text: @pytest.mark.langsmith
@pytest.fixture(langsmith=True)
@langsmith.evaluate
@traceable(test=True)

questions.explanation: Every test decorated with @pytest.mark.langsmith is synced to a dataset example, and each run creates an experiment with one result per test case.

questions.title: Which feedback keys does the LangSmith result of this test contain?
questions.codeSnippet:
@pytest.mark.langsmith
def test_sql() -> None:
    t.log_inputs({"user_query": "all users"})
    sql = generate_sql("all users")
    t.log_outputs({"sql": sql})
    t.log_feedback(key="valid_sql", score=is_valid_sql(sql))
    assert "customers" in sql

options.text: Only valid_sql
pass and valid_sql
Only pass
None, because no reference outputs were logged

questions.explanation: LangSmith records a default boolean pass feedback key from the test result, and log_feedback adds the custom valid_sql key. Reference outputs are optional.

questions.title: Fill in the blank so expected_sql is logged as the reference output rather than as an input.

options.text: reference_keys
expected
outputs
output_keys

questions.explanation: By default, all test arguments are logged as example inputs. output_keys names the arguments that represent reference outputs.

questions.title: An online evaluator is set to a sampling rate of 0.1. What does this mean?

options.text: It evaluates 10% of the runs that match the evaluator's filter
It evaluates every run but scores only the first 10 tokens
It runs once every 0.1 seconds
It evaluates 0.1% of all runs in the workspace

questions.explanation: The sampling rate controls the percentage of filtered runs that trigger the evaluator, which is a common way to control LLM-judge cost.

questions.title: When can you apply an online evaluator to past runs?

options.text: At any time by editing the existing rule
Only when you create the rule, using the apply-to-past-runs-from-date option
Never; online evaluators only see new traces
Only after the project is deleted and recreated

questions.explanation: Backfill is configured in the Advanced section while creating the rule and cannot be added later. It runs as a background job, after which the rule keeps evaluating new runs.

questions.title: Which environment variables does the LangSmith pytest integration support?

options.text: LANGSMITH_TEST_SUITE to name the test suite
LANGSMITH_EXPERIMENT to name the experiment
LANGSMITH_EXPERIMENT_METADATA to attach JSON metadata to the experiment
LANGSMITH_TEST_THRESHOLD to fail CI when the pass rate drops

questions.explanation: The docs describe suite name, experiment name and experiment metadata variables. There is no pass-rate threshold variable; failures come from assertions in the tests.

questions.title: Which statements about annotation queues are correct?

options.text: A single-run queue lets reviewers submit rubric feedback on runs or threads
A pairwise queue is created by selecting exactly two experiments in a dataset
A reviewed run can be saved as a dataset example with Add to Dataset
With several reviewers per run, each reviewer can see the others' feedback

questions.explanation: Reviewers cannot see feedback left by other reviewers, although comments are visible to everyone. The other statements match the annotation queue workflow.
